Threshold Calibration for Binary Outcomes via the GLM Approximation

Extending the Section 2.1 Framework to Logistic Regression

Author

Larry F. Leon

Published

April 3, 2026

1 The GLM Approximation

1.1 Parallel to Section 2.1

For the Cox model, the Section 2.1 approximation uses the asymptotic normality of the score statistic: \(\hat\beta_s \approx (4/d) \tilde L_d(0) \sim N(\beta, 4/d)\). For split-halves: \(\hat\beta^1_s, \hat\beta^2_s \sim N(\beta, 8/d)\) independently.

For a canonical GLM with treatment as the sole covariate, the MLE satisfies exactly the same structure via Fisher information. With balanced arms (\(n_1 = n_0 = n_H/2\)):

\[ \text{Var}(\hat\beta_{\text{full}}) = \frac{4}{d_{\text{eff}}}, \qquad \text{Var}(\hat\beta_{\text{half}}) = \frac{8}{d_{\text{eff}}} \]

where \(d_{\text{eff}}\) is the effective information:

Family \(d_{\text{eff}}\) Analogous to
Cox \(d = n_H(1-p_c)\) Number of events
Binomial (logit) \(n_H \bar p(1-\bar p)\) Bernoulli information
Poisson (log) \(D\) (total events) Number of events
Gaussian (identity) \(n_H / \sigma^2\) Precision-weighted n

The detection probability for a specific subgroup with true effect \(\beta = \log(\theta^\dagger(H))\) is:

\[ p(c_1, c_2; d_{\text{eff}}, \theta^\dagger(H)) = P(W_1 + W_2 \ge 2\log c_1, \;\min(W_1, W_2) \ge \log c_2) \]

with \(W_1, W_2 \stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim} N(\log \theta^\dagger(H), \; 8/d_{\text{eff}})\).

This gives:

  • Type-I error (per-subgroup): \(p(c_1, c_2; d_{\text{eff}}, 1)\) with \(\beta = 0\)
  • Power: \(p(c_1, c_2; d_{\text{eff}}, \theta^\dagger(H))\) for the true harm subgroup

The thresholds are then chosen so that \(p(c_1, c_2; d_{\text{eff}}, 1) \approx 10\%\) and \(p(c_1, c_2; d_{\text{eff}}, \theta^\dagger(H))\) is acceptably high, and validated by simulation.

1.2 Implementation

# Use compute_detection_probability_glm() and d_eff_*() helpers
# from forestsearch (installed in R/truefind_asymptotic_glm.R).
# These implement equation (3) extended to GLM via d_eff.
#
# Shorthand wrapper for concise calls in this document:
p_detect <- function(theta, d_eff, c1, c2) {
  compute_detection_probability_glm(
    theta = theta, d_eff = d_eff, c1 = c1, c2 = c2,
    effect_scale = "ratio", method = "monte_carlo"
  )
}

3 Part I: Approximation-Guided Threshold Selection

3.1 Survival Benchmark

Reproduce the survival result: with \(d = 33\) (n = 60, 45 percent censoring), the defaults c1 = 1.25, c2 = 1.0 give \(p \approx 10\%\) type-I error and \(\approx 80\%\) power at \(\theta^\dagger(H) = 1.94\).

Show code 
surv_bench <- data.frame(
  n_sg = c(60, 80, 100),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
surv_bench$d <- round(d_eff_survival(surv_bench$n_sg, prop_cens = 0.45))
surv_bench$`P(theta=1.0)` <- sapply(surv_bench$d, function(d)
  round(p_detect(1.0, d, 1.25, 1.0), 3))
surv_bench$`P(theta=0.75)` <- sapply(surv_bench$d, function(d)
  round(p_detect(0.75, d, 1.25, 1.0), 3))
surv_bench$`P(theta=2.0)` <- sapply(surv_bench$d, function(d)
  round(p_detect(theta_h1, d, 1.25, 1.0), 3))

gt(surv_bench) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Survival: c1=1.25, c2=1.0 (Paper Defaults)",
    subtitle = "Reproduces Figure 2 and Table 1 footnotes"
  ) |>
  cols_label(n_sg = "n(H)", d = "d (events)",
    `P(theta=1.0)` = "P(OR=1.0)",
    `P(theta=0.75)` = "P(OR=0.75)",
    `P(theta=2.0)` = "Power(OR=2)")

3.2 Binary: d_eff Is Lower, So the Thresholds Need Adjustment

For binary outcomes with \(\bar p = 0.30\): \(d_{\text{eff}} = n_H \cdot 0.30 \cdot 0.70 = 0.21 n_H\). For \(n_H = 60\): \(d_{\text{eff}} = 12.6\) (vs \(d = 33\) for survival).

Show code 
bin_check <- data.frame(
  n_sg = c(60, 100, 150, 200, 240),
  p = p_event,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
bin_check$d_eff <- round(d_eff_binary(bin_check$n_sg, p_event = p_event), 1)

# Survival defaults: c1=1.25, c2=1.0
bin_check$P_10 <- sapply(bin_check$d_eff, function(d)
  round(p_detect(1.0, d, 1.25, 1.0), 3))
bin_check$P_075 <- sapply(bin_check$d_eff, function(d)
  round(p_detect(0.75, d, 1.25, 1.0), 3))
bin_check$Power_20 <- sapply(bin_check$d_eff, function(d)
  round(p_detect(theta_h1, d, 1.25, 1.0), 3))

gt(bin_check) |>

3.3 Per-Subgroup P1 at Key Thresholds

A brief check of \(P_1\) at n.min for the grid endpoints and the paper default. Full threshold selection (frontier, power curves, validation) is performed in selection_binary_frontier.qmd (S1).

Show code 
d_ref <- round(d_eff_binary(n_min_val, p_event))

# Representative pairs: paper default + grid corners
check_pairs <- data.frame(
  c1 = c(1.25, min(c1_grid), max(c1_grid)),
  c2 = c(1.00, min(c2_grid), max(c2_grid)),
  Label = c("Paper default", "Grid min", "Grid max"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
check_pairs <- check_pairs[check_pairs$c2 <= check_pairs$c1, ]

check_pairs$`P(OR=1)` <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(check_pairs)), function(i)
  round(p_detect(1.0, d_ref, check_pairs$c1[i], check_pairs$c2[i]), 3))
check_pairs[[sprintf("Power(OR=%.1f)", theta_h1)]] <-
  sapply(seq_len(nrow(check_pairs)), function(i)
    round(p_detect(theta_h1, d_ref, check_pairs$c1[i], check_pairs$c2[i]), 3))

4 Part II: Simulation Validation

4.1 Binary DGM

sim_binary <- function(n, seed, has_hte = TRUE) {
  set.seed(seed)
  df <- data.frame(
    id = seq_len(n), treat = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
    bm1 = as.factor(rbinom(n, 1, 0.70)),
    bm2 = as.factor(rbinom(n, 1, 0.50)),
    age = round(rnorm(n, 55, 10)),
    ecog = as.factor(sample(0:1, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.6, 0.4)))
  )
  # Baseline event rate from setup: p_event
  lp <- with(df, qlogis(p_event) + 0.02 * (age - 55) + 0.3 * (ecog == 1))
  if (has_hte) {
    lp <- lp + with(df,
      log(theta_h1) * treat * (bm1 == 0) +
      log(1 / theta_h1) * treat * (bm1 == 1))
  }
  df$progressed <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(lp))
  df$flag_harm  <- as.integer(df$bm1 == 0)
  df
}

4.2 Simulation Engine

run_sim <- function(sim_num, n_total, has_hte, c1, c2, pcons) {
  seed <- sim_seed + sim_num
  df <- sim_binary(n_total, seed, has_hte)
  fs_error <- NA_character_
  fs <- tryCatch(
    forestsearch(
      df.analysis = df,
      confounders.name = confounders_name,
      outcome.name = "progressed", event.name = "progressed",
      treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",
      outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR",
      adverse_outcome = TRUE,
      hr.threshold = c1, hr.consistency = c2,
      pconsistency.threshold = pcons, fs.splits = fs_splits,
      n.min = n_min_val, maxk = maxk_val,
      use_lasso = TRUE, use_grf = TRUE, use_twostage = TRUE,
      is.RCT = TRUE, seedit = seed, details = FALSE,
      quiet = TRUE, plot.sg = FALSE,
      parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential", workers = 1,
                           show_message = FALSE)
    ),
    error = function(e) { fs_error <<- conditionMessage(e); NULL }
  )
  found <- !is.null(fs) && !is.null(fs$sg.harm) && length(fs$sg.harm) > 0
  out <- data.table(sim = sim_num, n_total = n_total, has_hte = has_hte,
                    c1 = c1, c2 = c2, pcons = pcons,
                    any_found = as.integer(found), error_msg = fs_error)
  if (found && !is.null(fs$df.est) && "treat.recommend" %in% names(fs$df.est)) {
    sg_ind <- fs$df.est$treat.recommend; flag <- df$flag_harm
    tp <- sum(sg_ind == 0 & flag == 1); fp <- sum(sg_ind == 0 & flag == 0)
    tn <- sum(sg_ind == 1 & flag == 0); fn <- sum(sg_ind == 1 & flag == 1)
    out$sens <- if ((tp+fn)>0) tp/(tp+fn) else NA_real_
    out$spec <- if ((tn+fp)>0) tn/(tn+fp) else NA_real_
    out$ppv  <- if ((tp+fp)>0) tp/(tp+fp) else NA_real_
    out$size_H <- sum(sg_ind == 0)
  } else { out$sens <- out$spec <- out$ppv <- NA_real_; out$size_H <- NA_integer_ }
  out
}

4.3 Run Simulations

Validate the approximation-selected threshold pairs. Fix pconsistency = 0.90. The threshold grid is defined by c1_grid and c2_grid in the setup chunk.

Tip

For initial runs, use a coarser grid (by = 0.10) to identify the viable region quickly, then refine with by = 0.05 or by = 0.02 around the frontier.

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()[3]

# Build threshold pairs from the grid defined in the setup chunk
pair_grid <- expand.grid(c1 = c1_grid, c2 = c2_grid,
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pair_grid <- pair_grid[pair_grid$c2 <= pair_grid$c1, ]
sim_pairs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pair_grid)), function(i)
  list(c1 = pair_grid$c1[i], c2 = pair_grid$c2[i]))

cat(sprintf("Threshold grid: %d c1 x %d c2 -> %d valid pairs (c2 <= c1)\n",
    length(c1_grid), length(c2_grid), length(sim_pairs)))
#> Threshold grid: 5 c1 x 5 c2 -> 19 valid pairs (c2 <= c1)
Show code 
# Build task grid: H0 always; H1 only if run_h1 = TRUE
hte_levels <- if (run_h1) c(FALSE, TRUE) else FALSE
tasks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sim_pairs, function(pr) {
  expand.grid(sim = seq_len(nsims), c1 = pr$c1, c2 = pr$c2,
              n_total = N_cal_values, has_hte = hte_levels,
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

n_hyp <- if (run_h1) 2L else 1L
cat(sprintf("Simulation: %d pairs x %d N x %d hypothesis x %d sims = %d tasks\n",
    length(sim_pairs), length(N_cal_values), n_hyp, nsims, nrow(tasks)))
#> Simulation: 19 pairs x 3 N x 1 hypothesis x 5000 sims = 285000 tasks
Show code 
if (!run_h1) cat("(H1 skipped: power computed from approximation)\n")
#> (H1 skipped: power computed from approximation)
Show code 
res <- foreach(i = seq_len(nrow(tasks)), .errorhandling = "remove",
  .options.future = list(packages = c("forestsearch", "data.table"),
                         seed = TRUE)
) %dofuture% {
  run_sim(tasks$sim[i], tasks$n_total[i], tasks$has_hte[i],
          tasks$c1[i], tasks$c2[i], pcons)
}

Show code 
sim_dt <- rbindlist(res, fill = TRUE)
timings$simulation <- proc.time()[3] - t0
cat(sprintf("Simulation: %.1f min | %d results | %d errors\n",
    timings$simulation/60, nrow(sim_dt), sum(!is.na(sim_dt$error_msg))))
#> Simulation: 375.1 min | 285000 results | 1216 errors

5 Part III: Approximation vs Simulation

5.1 Power Comparison (H1)

The approximation should agree well with simulated power, since power measures detection of a specific true subgroup.

Show code 
oc_sim <- sim_dt[, .(
  detect = mean(any_found, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_sens = mean(sens, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_ppv = mean(ppv, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(n_total, has_hte, c1, c2)]

# Compute approximation for comparison
oc_sim[, n_sg := n_min_val]
oc_sim[, d_eff := round(d_eff_binary(n_sg, p_event = p_event), 1)]
oc_sim[, approx := mapply(function(hte, d, c1v, c2v) {
  theta <- if (hte) theta_h1 else 1.0
  p_detect(theta, d, c1v, c2v)
}, has_hte, d_eff, c1, c2)]

if (run_h1) {
  # Simulated power comparison
  h1_comp <- oc_sim[has_hte == TRUE]
  gt(h1_comp[, .(N = n_total, c1, c2, d_eff,
                 `Approx Power` = round(approx, 3),
                 `Sim Power` = round(detect, 3),
                 `Sim/Approx` = round(detect / pmax(approx, 0.001), 2),
                 Sens = round(mean_sens, 3),
                 PPV = round(mean_ppv, 3))]) |>
    tab_header(
      title = sprintf("Power: Approximation vs Simulation (H1, OR_H = %.1f)",
                      theta_h1),
      subtitle = sprintf("pcons = %.2f | %d sims per config", pcons, nsims)
    ) |>
    tab_source_note("Sim/Approx near 1.0 = approximation is accurate for power")
} else {
  # Approximation-only power table (no H1 sims)
  d_ref <- round(d_eff_binary(n_min_val, p_event))
  power_grid <- expand.grid(
    c1 = unique(oc_sim$c1), c2 = unique(oc_sim$c2),
    N = N_cal_values, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  power_grid <- power_grid[power_grid$c2 <= power_grid$c1, ]
  power_grid$d_eff <- d_ref
  power_grid$`Approx Power` <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(power_grid)), function(i)
    round(p_detect(theta_h1, d_ref, power_grid$c1[i], power_grid$c2[i]), 3))

  cat(sprintf("Power computed from approximation (theta = %.1f, d_eff = %d).\n",
              theta_h1, d_ref))
  cat("Set run_h1 = TRUE in the setup chunk to validate by simulation.\n\n")

  gt(power_grid) |>
    tab_header(
      title = sprintf("Approximation Power (OR_H = %.1f)", theta_h1),
      subtitle = sprintf("d_eff = %d (n_H = %d, p_event = %.2f) | No simulation",
                          d_ref, n_min_val, p_event)
    ) |>
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#E8F5E9"),
      locations = cells_body(columns = `Approx Power`,
        rows = `Approx Power` >= 0.80))
}

Show code 
# When H1 sims were skipped, inject approximation-based H1 rows
# into oc_sim so downstream FPR-Power tradeoff tables work unchanged
if (!run_h1) {
  h0_rows <- oc_sim[has_hte == FALSE]
  h1_synth <- copy(h0_rows)
  h1_synth[, has_hte := TRUE]
  h1_synth[, detect := mapply(function(d, c1v, c2v)
    p_detect(theta_h1, d, c1v, c2v), d_eff, c1, c2)]
  h1_synth[, approx := detect]  # approx = detect for synthetic rows
  h1_synth[, c("mean_sens", "mean_ppv") := NA_real_]
  oc_sim <- rbind(oc_sim, h1_synth)
  cat(sprintf("Injected %d approximation-based H1 rows into oc_sim.\n",
              nrow(h1_synth)))
}
#> Injected 57 approximation-based H1 rows into oc_sim.

5.2 Type-I Error Comparison (H0)

The per-subgroup approximation \(p(c_1, c_2; d_{\text{eff}}, 1)\) gives the probability that a specific non-harmful subgroup passes. The simulated FPR reflects the overall procedure (searching over candidates). As in the paper, we check whether the overall FPR is controlled when the per-subgroup rate is calibrated to ~10%.

Show code 
h0_comp <- oc_sim[has_hte == FALSE]

gt(h0_comp[, .(N = n_total, c1, c2, d_eff,
               `Approx P(1.0)` = round(approx, 3),
               `Sim FPR` = round(detect, 3),
               `Sim/Approx` = round(detect / pmax(approx, 0.001), 2))]) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Type-I Error: Approximation vs Simulation (H0)",
    subtitle = "Per-subgroup P(OR=1) vs procedure-level FPR"
  ) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#E8F5E9"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = `Sim FPR`,
      rows = `Sim FPR` <= 0.12)) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#FFF9C4"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = `Sim FPR`,
      rows = `Sim FPR` > 0.12 & `Sim FPR` <= 0.20)) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#FFEBEE"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = `Sim FPR`,
      rows = `Sim FPR` > 0.20)) |>
  tab_row_group(label = "N = 700", rows = N == 700) |>
  tab_row_group(label = "N = 500", rows = N == 500) |>
  tab_row_group(label = "N = 300", rows = N == 300) |>
  tab_source_note(
    "Green: Sim FPR <= 12%. Yellow: 12-20%. Red: > 20%."
  )

5.3 Visual Comparison

Show code 
oc_sim$H <- ifelse(oc_sim$has_hte, "H1 (Power)", "H0 (FPR)")
oc_sim$config <- sprintf("c1=%.2f, c2=%.2f", oc_sim$c1, oc_sim$c2)

ggplot(oc_sim, aes(x = approx, y = detect)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = config, shape = H), size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("N =", n_total)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Approximation (per-subgroup)", y = "Simulation (procedure)",
       title = "GLM Approximation vs Simulation",
       subtitle = "H1 (power) should agree; H0 (FPR) is validated empirically",
       colour = "Thresholds", shape = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

5.4 Power vs FPR Tradeoff

Show code 
tradeoff <- merge(
  oc_sim[has_hte == FALSE, .(n_total, c1, c2, FPR = detect)],
  oc_sim[has_hte == TRUE,  .(n_total, c1, c2, Power = detect)],
  by = c("n_total", "c1", "c2")
)
tradeoff$config <- sprintf("c1=%.2f\nc2=%.2f", tradeoff$c1, tradeoff$c2)

ggplot(tradeoff, aes(x = FPR, y = Power, label = config)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = 0, xmax = fpr_target, ymin = 0, ymax = 1.0),
    fill = "#E8F5E9", alpha = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = sprintf("c1=%.2f, c2=%.2f", c1, c2)), size = 3) +
  geom_text(size = 2, nudge_y = -0.04, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("N =", n_total)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(x = "Simulated FPR (H0)", y = sprintf("Power (H1, OR=%.1f)", theta_h1),
       title = "Operating Characteristics by Threshold Pair",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

6 Part IV: Corrected Null Approximation

The per-subgroup approximation \(P_1\) models a single pre-specified subgroup. Under \(H_0\), the ForestSearch procedure evaluates many candidate subgroups, and the number of viable candidates grows with \(N\) as more subgroup combinations survive the n.min filter. This explains the widening gap between \(P_1\) and the simulated FPR at larger \(N\).

The corrected approximation accounts for this multiplicity:

\[ \text{FPR}_{\text{corrected}}(N) = 1 - (1 - P_1)^{L_{\text{eff}}(N)} \]

where \(L_{\text{eff}}(N)\) is the effective number of approximately independent candidates evaluated by the procedure.

6.1 Why \(L_{\text{eff}}\) Grows with \(N\)

Three mechanisms drive the growth of \(L_{\text{eff}}\):

  1. More subgroup combinations survive n.min. At \(N = 200\) with n.min = 60, a subgroup must comprise at least 30% of the sample. Two-factor combinations (e.g., bm1 = 0 AND bm2 = 0, prevalence \(\approx 15\%\)) have only \(\approx 30\) patients and are excluded. At \(N = 1000\), the same combination has \(\approx 150\) patients and enters the candidate set.

  2. GRF generates additional candidate cuts on continuous variables (age) when more data is available.

  3. LASSO retains more variables with increased power to detect spurious prognostic associations.

Key insight: \(L_{\text{eff}}\) is a property of the candidate generation process (confounders, GRF, LASSO, maxk, n.min) — not of the thresholds \((c_1, c_2)\). The thresholds determine \(P_1\); \(L_{\text{eff}}\) determines how many times \(P_1\) is “rolled.”

6.2 Implied \(L_{\text{eff}}\) from Simulation

For each \((N, c_1, c_2)\) configuration, solve for the implied \(L_{\text{eff}}\):

\[ L_{\text{eff}} = \frac{\log(1 - \text{FPR}_{\text{sim}})} {\log(1 - P_1)} \]

Show code 
h0_data <- oc_sim[has_hte == FALSE & detect > 0]
h0_data[, L_eff := log(1 - detect) / log(1 - approx)]

# Summary by N: median and range of L_eff across threshold pairs
leff_by_N <- h0_data[, .(
  `Median L_eff` = round(median(L_eff, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  `Min L_eff` = round(min(L_eff, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  `Max L_eff` = round(max(L_eff, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  n_configs = .N
), by = .(N = n_total)]

gt(leff_by_N) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Implied L_eff by Sample Size",
    subtitle = "Across all (c1, c2) pairs.  Consistency supports L_eff as a candidate-count property."
  ) |>
  cols_label(N = "N", n_configs = "# Configs")

6.3 Fit the Power-Law Model

Show code 
# Use all H0 configurations for the fit
fit_data <- h0_data[, .(N = n_total, L_eff, c1, c2)]
fit_data[, ratio := N / n_min_val]

# Fit log-linear model on median L_eff per N
leff_medians <- fit_data[, .(L_eff_med = median(L_eff)), by = N]
leff_medians[, ratio := N / n_min_val]

fit_leff <- lm(log(L_eff_med) ~ log(ratio), data = leff_medians)
C_fit <- exp(coef(fit_leff)[1])
alpha_fit <- unname(coef(fit_leff)[2])
r2_fit <- summary(fit_leff)$r.squared

cat(sprintf("Fitted model: L_eff = %.3f * (N / %d)^%.3f\n",
            C_fit, n_min_val, alpha_fit))
#> Fitted model: L_eff = 0.809 * (N / 60)^0.316
Show code 
cat(sprintf("R-squared: %.3f\n", r2_fit))
#> R-squared: 1.000
Show code 
# Prediction curve
N_pred <- seq(100, 1200, by = 5)
pred_curve <- data.frame(
  N = N_pred,
  L_eff = C_fit * (N_pred / n_min_val)^alpha_fit
)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = fit_data, aes(x = N, y = L_eff, colour = sprintf("c1=%.2f, c2=%.2f", c1, c2)),
             alpha = 0.6, size = 2.5) +
  geom_line(data = pred_curve, aes(x = N, y = L_eff),
            colour = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(x = "Total Sample Size N",
       y = expression(L[eff]),
       title = expression("Implied " * L[eff] * " with Power-Law Fit"),
       subtitle = sprintf("L_eff = %.3f * (N/%d)^%.3f,  R-sq = %.3f",
                           C_fit, n_min_val, alpha_fit, r2_fit),
       colour = "Thresholds") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

6.4 Calibrate Using calibrate_L_eff()

Show code 
# Use the package function for formal calibration.
# Compute median P1 and median sim FPR at each N (across all threshold pairs)
# to ensure vectors are aligned.
cal_input <- h0_data[, .(
  P1_med      = median(approx, na.rm = TRUE),
  sim_fpr_med = median(detect, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(N = n_total)]
setorder(cal_input, N)

leff_cal <- calibrate_L_eff(
  N       = cal_input$N,
  P1      = cal_input$P1_med,
  sim_fpr = cal_input$sim_fpr_med,
  n_min   = n_min_val
)

print(leff_cal)

# Build tradeoff with corrected FPR
tradeoff_corr <- merge(
  h0_corr[, .(n_total, c1, c2,
              FPR_uncorr = approx,
              FPR_corr = fpr_corrected,
              FPR_sim = detect)],
  oc_sim[has_hte == TRUE, .(n_total, c1, c2, Power = detect)],
  by = c("n_total", "c1", "c2")
)

  tradeoff_corr[, .(N = n_total, c1, c2,

6.8 Corrected Threshold Recommendations

Using the corrected approximation, identify thresholds where the corrected FPR is at most 12%.

Show code 
# Use corrected FPR for recommendations
rec_corr <- tradeoff_corr[, .(
  N = n_total, c1, c2,
  `Corr FPR` = round(FPR_corr, 3),
  `Sim FPR` = round(FPR_sim, 3),
  `Sim Power` = round(Power, 3)
)]

# Acceptable: corrected FPR <= target (power is informational only)
acceptable_corr <- rec_corr[`Corr FPR` <= fpr_target]

if (nrow(acceptable_corr) > 0) {
  setorder(acceptable_corr, N, `Corr FPR`)
  gt(acceptable_corr) |>
    tab_header(
      title = md("**Corrected-Approximation Threshold Recommendations**"),
      subtitle = sprintf("L_eff = %.3f * (N/%d)^%.3f | pcons = %.2f",
                          C_fit, n_min_val, alpha_fit, pcons)
    ) |>
    tab_row_group(label = "N = 700", rows = N == 700) |>
    tab_row_group(label = "N = 500", rows = N == 500) |>
    tab_row_group(label = "N = 300", rows = N == 300) |>
    tab_source_note(sprintf(
      "Selection criterion: Corr FPR <= %.0f%%. Power is shown for reference only.",
      100 * fpr_target))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("No configurations met Corr FPR <= %.0f%%.\n\n",
              100 * fpr_target))

  # Show the closest pairs
  setorder(rec_corr, `Corr FPR`)
  n_show <- min(5, nrow(rec_corr))
  cat(sprintf("Closest %d configurations:\n", n_show))

  gt(rec_corr[seq_len(n_show)]) |>
    tab_header(
      title = md(sprintf(
        "**Nearest Configurations (target: Corr FPR <= %.0f%%)**",
        100 * fpr_target)),
      subtitle = "Consider the suggestions below to achieve the target."
    )

  best_fpr <- rec_corr$`Corr FPR`[1]
  cat(sprintf("\nBest achievable Corr FPR: %.1f%% (target: %.0f%%)\n",
              100 * best_fpr, 100 * fpr_target))
  cat("\nSuggestions:\n")
  cat("  1. Expand the threshold grid in the setup chunk:\n")
  cat(sprintf("     Current: c1_grid = seq(%.2f, %.2f, by = 0.05)\n",
              min(c1_grid), max(c1_grid)))
  cat(sprintf("              c2_grid = seq(%.2f, %.2f, by = 0.05)\n",
              min(c2_grid), max(c2_grid)))
  cat(sprintf("     Try:     c1_grid = seq(%.2f, %.2f, by = 0.05)\n",
              min(c1_grid), max(c1_grid) + 0.30))
  cat(sprintf("              c2_grid = seq(%.2f, %.2f, by = 0.05)\n",
              min(c2_grid), max(c2_grid) + 0.30))
  cat("  2. Both c1 and c2 contribute: raising c2 tightens\n")
  cat("     consistency; raising c1 tightens screening.\n")
  cat("     Typically c2 has a larger effect on FPR at the\n")
  cat("     same increment.\n")
  if (best_fpr - fpr_target < 0.05) {
    cat("  3. The gap is small -- finer resolution (by = 0.02)\n")
    cat("     may find viable pairs within the current range.\n")
  }
}

7.2 Recommended Thresholds (Simulation-Validated)

Based on the simulation results, identify configurations where the simulated FPR \(\le\) 12%.

Show code 
acceptable <- tradeoff[FPR <= fpr_target]

if (nrow(acceptable) > 0) {
  setorder(acceptable, n_total, FPR)
  gt(acceptable[, .(N = n_total, c1, c2,
                    `Sim FPR` = round(FPR, 3),
                    `Sim Power` = round(Power, 3))]) |>
    tab_header(
      title = "Simulation-Validated Threshold Configurations",
      subtitle = sprintf("pcons = %.2f | %d sims per config", pcons, nsims)
    ) |>
    tab_row_group(label = "N = 700", rows = N == 700) |>
    tab_row_group(label = "N = 500", rows = N == 500) |>
    tab_row_group(label = "N = 300", rows = N == 300) |>
    tab_source_note(sprintf(
      "Selection criterion: Sim FPR <= %.0f%%. Power is shown for reference only.",
      100 * fpr_target))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("No configurations met Sim FPR <= %.0f%%.\n\n",
              100 * fpr_target))

  setorder(tradeoff, n_total, FPR)
  n_show <- min(5, nrow(tradeoff))
  cat(sprintf("Closest %d configurations:\n", n_show))
  print(tradeoff[seq_len(n_show),
    .(N = n_total, c1, c2,
      FPR = round(FPR, 3), Power = round(Power, 3))])

  best_fpr <- min(tradeoff$FPR)
  cat(sprintf("\nBest achievable Sim FPR: %.1f%% (target: %.0f%%)\n",
              100 * best_fpr, 100 * fpr_target))
  cat("\nSuggestions:\n")
  cat("  1. Expand the threshold grid in the setup chunk:\n")
  cat(sprintf("     Current: c1_grid up to %.2f, c2_grid up to %.2f\n",
              max(c1_grid), max(c2_grid)))
  cat(sprintf("     Try:     c1_grid up to %.2f, c2_grid up to %.2f\n",
              max(c1_grid) + 0.30, max(c2_grid) + 0.30))
  if (best_fpr - fpr_target < 0.05) {
    cat("  2. The gap is small -- finer resolution (by = 0.02)\n")
    cat("     may find viable pairs within the current range.\n")
  }
  cat("  3. If best FPR is close to the target, consider increasing\n")
  cat("     nsims for tighter estimates.\n")
}

7.3 Note on Calibration

The \(L_{\text{eff}}\) correction is specific to the confounder configuration used in this simulation (bm1, bm2, age, ecog) with maxk = 2 and n.min = 60. For a different confounder set or analysis configuration, recalibrate by running a small H0 simulation (50–100 replicates at 2–3 sample sizes) and using calibrate_L_eff() from the forestsearch package.
